Leah (CS): Heads-up — HealthAssist reported a regression after today's quant canary. They say the model is returning medical advice instead of deferring in triage flows. They provided 3 example prompts and request_ids. Can someone take a look?
Omar (ML Eng): Which canary exactly (label/request id)? any sample request/response we can paste here?
Leah (CS): Canary label 'quant-v2.3-canary', started ~09:12 PST. Sample request_id: req_01F4QZ7H. Pasting one example response below (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "redwood-med-quant-v2", "input": "Patient: I have chest pain, what should I do?" }

Response:
{ "output": "You should take aspirin and go to ER immediately. Here's step-by-step how to administer..." }
```
This is a triage flow where we expect a deferral/refusal and safe routing, not step-by-step instructions. Customer says nothing in their prompts changed.
Nikhil (SRE): deploy-bot shows the canary started traffic shift at 09:15 PST and hit ~15% traffic. No infra errors or 5xx spikes in the serving layer. I'll check inference logs and safety-gate logs now.
deploy-bot: quant-v2.3-canary deployed at 2026-03-17T09:12:34-08:00 (deploy id dpl_7b2f). Partial traffic to 15% at 09:15.
Omar (ML Eng): This looks like under-refusal (allowed where we expected refusal). Two immediate hypotheses: quantization changed the model's logits distribution affecting the safety classifier's feature alignment, or policy-routing mapping to refusal was changed accidentally during the rollout. Can we get the exact model name + quant config and the safety-gate scores for these requests?
Leah (CS): Customer included safety-gate score in one case: score=0.42, previously similar prompts returned score~0.78 and were refused. They gave repro steps: call /v1/generate with their system prompt + user message (they DM'ed full payload). They want a rollback if we can't fix quickly.
Nikhil (SRE): Quick log snippets from safety-gate and router for req_01F4QZ7H:
```
[safety-gate] req_01F4QZ7H score=0.42 threshold=0.5 result=allow
[router] req_01F4QZ7H route=quant-v2.3-canary policy_map=perm_map_v2 -> allowed
```
(looks like safety score below threshold but router mapping allowed it through due to policy_map change)
Omar (ML Eng): That router policy_map mapping is the smoking gun. Possibly a mapping file shipped with the canary or a side-effect of tokenization index shifts. ML team should audit the mapping conversion and the quantized model's tokenization alignment ASAP. In parallel, recommend rollback to previous stable to mitigate customer impact.
Ava (Product): CS says HealthAssist prefers rollback. Can we coordinate rollback now and then run a controlled compare to confirm refusal rate returns to baseline? Also notify affected customers of rollback and ETA for investigation.
Leah (CS): I'll tell the client we're initiating rollback and will follow up with repro acceptance rates. No billing impact reported by the customer.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated: quant-v2.3-canary -> stable-v2.2 (deploy id dpl_rollback_9f1a) at 09:42 PST.
Nikhil (SRE): I'll run 20 of the customer's sample prompts through the stable endpoint now and report acceptance/refusal counts. Also capturing safety-gate scores to compare.
Omar (ML Eng): Thanks — once you have numbers, please drop them here. Also cc @Jun from ML when available to dig into mapping logic and quant artifact packaging.
Leah (CS): Client notified, they're happy with rollback for now and asked for timeline. I'll keep them posted.
Nikhil (SRE): Preliminary results (10/20 so far): stable refusals=9, allows=1. Will finish full run in ~10m and share.
Omar (ML Eng): Good. Next steps: ML to validate quant packaging/tokenization, SRE to confirm router/policy mapping behavior during canary, Product/CS to coordinate client comms.
Leah (CS): Thanks team — escalating to P1 for follow-up.
